headline: Zoning Board approves deck, driveway, garage, and duplex variances across six Nashua addresses; one variance request withdrawn
summary: The Zoning Board of Adjustment heard seven cases involving variances and special exceptions for properties including 12 Brinton Drive, 12 Annabelle Court, East Hobart Street, 568 S. Main Street, 30 Merrimack Street, 19 Dublin Avenue, and 19 Cross Street. Most requests were approved, one variance application was withdrawn after the Board found it unnecessary, and July 28, 2026 minutes were approved as amended.
decisions: Approved the special exception for 12 Brinton Drive to work in the wetland buffer and replace a deck, 4-0.
Approved the variance for 12 Annabelle Court to exceed maximum driveway width up to 29 feet, 4-0.
Determined that the frontage and width variances for 'L' East Hobart Street were not required, 4-0.
The variance applications for East Hobart Street were withdrawn without prejudice.
Approved the special exception for a duplex at East Hobart Street, 3-1 with Mr. Minkarah opposed.
Approved the variance for 568 S. Main Street to exceed maximum accessory use area to 50.8% for a shed, 4-0.
Approved the variance for 30 Merrimack Street to exceed accessory use area to 78% for a three-car garage, 3-0.
Approved the variance for 19 Dublin Avenue to allow a driveway 38 feet from an intersection, 4-0.
Approved the variance for 19 Cross Street allowing conversion to five units instead of six, 4-0.
Approved the July 28, 2026 minutes as amended, 4-0.

EXPANDED DRAFT MEETING SUMMARY

THE INFORMATION CONTAINED HEREIN HAS NOT BEEN REVIEWED OR APPROVED BY THE ZBA 
 
 
ZONING BOARD OF ADJUSTMENT PUBLIC HEARING AND MEETING  
Tuesday, August 11, 2026 
 
A public hearing of the Zoning Board of Adjustment was held on 
Tuesday, August 11, 2026, at 6:30 PM, in the 3rd floor auditorium 
at Nashua City Hall, 229 Main Street, Nashua, NH. 
 
Jay Minkarah, Chair, asked for a Roll Call: 
 
Jay Minkarah, Chair 
JP Boucher, Member 
Steve Lionel, Member 
Joseph Patry, Member 
 
Sam Durfee, Planning Manager 
 
Mr. Minkarah noted that Vice Chair Josh Nehiley was not present 
for the evening. 
 
Mr. Minkarah explained the Board's procedures, stating that the 
public is invited to present case s within a fifteen -minute 
timeframe. He encouraged the public to submit comments for future 
meetings via email to the Planning Department at zb@nashuanh.gov 
or by mail to P.O. Box 2019, Nashua, NH, 03061. He identified the 
points of law required for applic ants to address relative to 
variances and special exceptions. A special exception is a use 
allowed under the ordinance provided specific criteria are met. 
For a variance, Mr. Minkarah explained that the Board must find 
five specific criteria are met: that the variance would not be 
contrary to the public interest, the spirit of the ordinance would 
be observed, substantial justice would be done, no diminution of 
surrounding property values would occur, and that an unnecessary 
hardship exists due to special co nditions of the property. Mr. 
Minkarah explained the order of testimony, including the 
applicant’s presentation, speakers in favor, speakers in 
opposition or with concerns, and the applicant’s final five-minute 
rebuttal. 
 
Mr. Minkarah announced the case at 38 Buckmeadow is postponed to 
the August 25, 2026 meeting. 
 
1. Kathleen Yourell Wallace Rev. Living Trust, Kathleen Yourell 
Wallace, Trustee (Owner) 12 Brinton Drive (Sheet 49 Lot 224) 
requesting special exception from Land Use Code Section 190-112 to
Zoning Board of Adjustment 
August 11, 2026 
Page 2 
 
 
 
work in 75-foot prime wetland buffer of Supply Pond to replace an 
existing 10’x12’ deck with a new 12’ x 24’ deck. RA Zone, Ward 2. 
 
Voting on this case: 
 
Jay Minkarah 
JP Boucher 
Steve Lionel 
Joseph Patry 
 
Kathleen Wallace, 12 Brinton Drive, Nashua, NH.  Ms. Wallace 
clarified that the existing deck is already 12’x24’, rather than 
the 10’x12’ footprint stated in the application. She stated she 
has lived at the property for over 25 years and the deck is now 
rotting and requires an update. She noted that to bring the 
structure up to current permit codes, she must adjust the footings 
from 8 inches to 12 inches. She confirmed that the new deck would 
occupy the same footprint as the original. Ms. Wallace stated that 
the Conservation Commission reviewed the project in July and 
provided a favorable recommendation with no stipulations. 
 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR:  
No one. 
 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR WITH QUESTIONS OR CONCERNS:  
No one. 
 
END OF PUBLIC HEARING, BEGINNING OF PUBLIC MEETING:  
The Board’s deliberation was concise given the nature of the 
request. Mr. Boucher spoke in support of the application, noting 
that the deck is a long -standing existing structure. He observed 
that doing a drive-by of the neighborhood and reviewing GIS maps 
confirms that most homes on that side of the street contend with 
the same wetland buffer issues. He stated that the applicant has 
no other choice for placement and that replacing a rotting deck is 
a matter of safety. Mr. Minkarah noted that the applicant h ad 
signed the stipulation regarding special conditions for wetland 
work. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Boucher to approve the special exception application 
on behalf of the owner as advertised, noting the correction that 
the existing deck is 12’x24’. 
 
Mr. Boucher stated that the requested use is listed in the special 
exception matrix and is permitted under Section 190-112.
Zoning Board of Adjustment 
August 11, 2026 
Page 3 
 
 
 
 
Mr. Boucher stated the requested use will not create undue traffic 
congestion or unduly impair pedestrian safety  as it is a private 
residential deck. 
 
Mr. Boucher stated the requested use will not overload any public 
water, drainage, or sewer system or any other municipal system to 
such an extent that the area will be subjected to hazards affecting 
health or safety. 
 
Mr. Boucher stated that all special re gulations have been 
fulfilled, including the nine individual wetland special 
conditions attested to and signed off by the applicant. 
 
Mr. Boucher stated the requested use will not impair the integrity 
or be out of character with the neighborhood , nor be detrimental 
to the health, morals, or welfare of residents, specifically citing 
the favorable recommendation from the Conservation Commission 
dated July 9th. 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Lionel.  
MOTION TO APPROVE CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY 4-0. 
 
 
2. The Kumar Family Rev. Liv. Trust (Owners) 12 Annabelle Court 
(Sheet C Lot 2900) requesting variance from Land Use Code Section 
190-17 (E)(2) to exceed maximum driveway width, 24 feet permitted 
– up to 29 feet proposed, for a driveway addition on right side of 
existing driveway. R40/FUOD Zone, Ward 9. 
 
Voting on this case: 
 
Jay Minkarah 
JP Boucher 
Steve Lionel 
Joseph Patry 
 
Amit Kumar, 12 Annabelle Court, Nashua, NH. Dr. Kumar stated that 
he and his family built the home 16 years ago. He explained that 
as his children have reached high school age, the family now 
requires a third vehicle. The current driveway is approximately 20 
feet wide with a two -car garage. He is requesting to widen the 
upper portion of the driveway near the garage to 29 feet while 
leaving the entrance at the street unchanged.
Zoning Board of Adjustment 
August 11, 2026 
Page 4 
 
 
 
Dr. Kumar emphasized that safety and snow management are the 
primary drivers for the request. He noted the driveway has a 
significant slope and that his medical practice at Foundation 
Medical almost never cancels due to weather, requiring him to clear 
snow early in the morning to get to work on time. The extra width 
would allow him to park a car to the side to facilitate safer and 
more efficient passes with a snowblower. He proposed constructing 
a professional retaining wall with appropriate drainage to protect 
both his property and the neighbor's property. Dr. Kumar submitted 
a letter of support from his neighbor at 14 Annabelle Court. He 
noted the garage is approximately 48 feet back from the street. 
 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR:  
No one. 
 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR WITH QUESTIONS OR CONCERNS:  
No one. 
 
END OF PUBLIC HEARING, BEGINNING OF PUBLIC MEETING:  
The Board's deliberation focused on the site-specific challenges. 
Mr. Lionel stated that while he is generally not a fan of widening 
driveways, the request is minimal and reasonable given the slope 
and the neighbor's agreement. Mr. Boucher noted the unique geometry 
of the property, which is situated on a circle (cul -de-sac). He 
observed that the driveway is located on the shortest distance to 
the house, which creates a unique constraint. Mr. Minkarah agreed, 
noting that the angle of the house and the curb distance make the 
property appear closer to the front property line than is typical. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Lionel to approve the variance application on behalf 
of the owner as advertised. 
 
Mr. Lionel stated that granting the variance would not be contrary 
to the public interest as it improves safety for the homeowner and 
has no deleterious effect on neighbors, as confirmed by testimony 
from the affected abutter. 
 
Mr. Lionel stated the spirit of the ordinance would be observed  
because the limited scope and design of the addition will not be 
visually imposing or detract from the neighborhood's aesthetic. 
 
Mr. Lionel stated that substantial justice  will be served  by 
allowing the applicant to move vehicles safely to clear snow, 
allowing for essential medical work travel.
Zoning Board of Adjustment 
August 11, 2026 
Page 5 
 
 
 
Mr. Lionel stated the Board has no evidence that property values 
would be diminished. 
 
Mr. Lionel stated that unnecessary hardship exists due to special 
conditions of the property, specifically its location on a 
circle/cul-de-sac and the side-sloping topography. He found there 
is no fair and substantial relationship between the general public 
purpose of the ordinance and its specific application here. 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Patry.  
MOTION TO APPROVE CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY 4-0. 
 
 
3. Edward J. Paquin, Trustee of the Edward J. Paquin Revocable 
Trust (Owner) “L” East Hobart Street (Sheet 129 Lot 13) requesting 
variances for: 1) minimum lot frontage, 60 feet required, 37 feet 
proposed; 2) minimum lot width, 75 feet required, 51 feet proposed; 
and 3) special exception from Land Use Code Section 190 -156 to 
allow a duplex residential building. RA Zone, Ward 7. 
 
Voting on this case: 
 
Jay Minkarah 
JP Boucher 
Steve Lionel 
Joseph Patry 
 
PRE-HEARING BOARD DISCUSSION:  
Before opening the public hearing, the Board engaged in a detailed 
discussion regarding the necessity of the requested variances for 
lot width and frontage. Mr. Minkarah noted that since this is an 
existing lot of record and n ot a new subdivision, the proposed 
dimensions are inherent to the land. The Board reviewed a staff 
memo from Mr. Durfee. Mr. Lionel and Mr. Boucher agreed it seemed 
inappropriate to penalize a landowner for dimensional issues that 
existed prior to current zoning codes, provided the proposed 
building fits within all other setbacks. Mr. Patry cited Land Use 
Code Section 190 -121, which he interpreted as making such non -
conforming lots essentially conforming for development purposes. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Minkarah that  the two variances for frontage and 
width are not required based on Section 190-121 and the fact that 
the lot is an existing lot of record.  
 
SECONDED by Mr. Patry.
Zoning Board of Adjustment 
August 11, 2026 
Page 6 
 
 
 
MOTION CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY 4-0. 
Brad Westgate, attorney with Whelts, White & Fontaine, 
representing Ed Paquin.  Attorney Westgate formally withdrew the 
variance applications without prejudice following the Board’s 
determination. 
 
Regarding the special exception for the duplex, Attorney Westgate 
stated the lot is approximately 29,000 square feet, nea rly four 
times the minimum size requirement for the RA district. He 
described the project as ideal "infill development". He noted that 
while a single-family home could be built by right, the duplex is 
permitted by special exception. The proposed building would be set 
back roughly 200 feet from East Hobart Street, making it "nestled" 
among other properties and largely invisible from the street. 
 
Attorney Westgate addressed neighbor concerns regarding drainage, 
stating that the applicant would handle drainage appropriately 
through the building and tie -in permit processes. He noted the 
property contains a brook that is part of a larger watershed, and 
the project would honor all wetland setbacks. He clarified that 
the proposed 60’x40’ structural box on the plan was conceptual to 
establish a maximum footprint. 
 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR:  
A letter of support was read from David and Ann Pfeiffer, 12 East 
Hobart Street, stating the project would add value to the 
neighborhood. 
 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR WITH QUESTIONS OR CONCERNS:  
Brice Young, 11 East Hobart Street.  Mrs. Young expressed concern 
regarding the size of the project and the significant percentage 
of relief originally requested. She highlighted existing issues 
with standing water and mosquitoes in her yard and asked ho w 
stormwater runoff would be handled. She also cited concerns 
regarding construction noise, dust, and the loss of privacy 
provided by existing trees. Mrs. Young noted that the city's 
assessing records label the parcel as "undevelopable". 
 
Robert Goldman, 19 Dudley Street. Mr. Goldman stated his property 
is at the end of the brook's line. He expressed concern that an 
impervious structure of this size would increase water deflection 
and exacerbate the existing flooding in his backyard, which 
occurred during the massive storms of 2023. 
 
A letter from Christina Torres Scarlatos, 1 East Hobart Street,
Zoning Board of Adjustment 
August 11, 2026 
Page 7 
 
 
 
cited concerns regarding neighborhood character intensity, 
traffic, road capacity, and construction disruption. 
 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR – REBUTTAL:  
Attorney Westgate reiter ated that Mr. Paquin would work through 
the Community Development Division to ensure drainage is handled 
properly and noted that the applicant must protect his own property 
from water damage as well. 
 
END OF PUBLIC HEARING, BEGINNING OF PUBLIC MEETING:  
Mr. Durfee clarified that while duplexes do not go to the Planning 
Board, drainage standards are considered "peripherally" through 
the engineering review during the building permit process. Mr. 
Lionel stated that the massive setback of the house from the street 
made him feel better about the proposal. Mr. Patry and Mr. Boucher 
agreed that since a single-family home could be built in the same 
footprint without ZBA approval, the construction and character 
concerns were less weighty than the fact that the use is reasonable 
for the lot size. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Boucher to approve the special exception application. 
 
Mr. Boucher stated the requested use is listed as a special 
exception in the use matrix. 
 
Mr. Boucher stated the requested use will not create undue traffic 
congestion or unduly impair pedestrian safety. 
 
Mr. Boucher stated the requested use will not overload any public 
water, drainage, or sewer system , noting that the builder must 
ensure runoff does not increase to surrounding properties. 
Mr. Boucher stated there are no special regulations to be 
fulfilled. 
 
Mr. Boucher stated the requested use will not impair the integrity 
or character of the neighborhood given its significant setback and 
its location in a residential district. 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Patry.  
MOTION TO APPROVE CARRIED 3-1. Mr. Minkarah in opposition. 
 
 
4. Nathan Delyani (Owner) Kelsie Delyani (Applicant) 568 S. Main 
Street (Sheet A Lot 114) requesting variance from Land Use Code 
Section 190-264 to exceed maximum accessory use area, 40% permitted
Zoning Board of Adjustment 
August 11, 2026 
Page 8 
 
 
 
– 50.8% proposed – to construct a 120 sq.ft shed. RA Zone, Ward 7. 
Voting on this case: 
 
Jay Minkarah 
JP Boucher 
Steve Lionel 
Joseph Patry 
 
Kelsie Delyani, 568 South Main Street, Nashua, NH.  Mrs. Delyani 
stated the home is just under 1,500 square feet on a large 0.7 -
acre lot. Because the house is relatively small for the lot size, 
the addition of a 120 -square-foot freestanding shed exceeds the 
40% accessory use area limit. She noted the lot is wooded and 
private, making the shed invisible from the street and neighbors. 
She clarified the unique nature of the lot, explaining that it is 
accessed via a right -of-way and that the land between her house 
and South Main Street is owned by the Osgood family. She confirmed 
that the neighbor who initially expressed concern had visited the 
property, reviewed the lines, and now supports the project. 
 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR:  
No one. 
 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR WITH QUESTIONS OR CONCERNS:  
No one. 
 
END OF PUBLIC HEARING, BEGINNING OF PUBLIC MEETING:  
Mr. Lionel noted this is a typical request for a small house on a 
large lot with a detached garage. Mr. Minkarah agreed the shed 
size is conventional and the lot is unusual. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Patry to approve the variance application. 
 
Mr. Patry stated that granting the variance would not be contrary 
to the public interest as the shed size is minor relative to the 
lot and allows the owner to fully utilize the property. 
 
Mr. Patry stated the spirit of the ordinance would be observed  
because the shed does not harm neighborhood character or impact 
neighbors. 
 
Mr. Patry stated that substantial justice will be served  by 
allowing the owner storage space that is otherwise limited by the 
house's layout.
Zoning Board of Adjustment 
August 11, 2026 
Page 9 
 
 
 
Mr. Patry stated property values will not be diminished due to the 
wooded screening and lack of impact. 
 
Mr. Patry stated that unnecessary hardship exists  due to the 
special conditions of the property’s size versus the home’s small 
footprint. He noted the proposed use is reasonable and typical for 
the area. 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Boucher.  
MOTION TO APPROVE CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY 4-0. 
 
 
5. Robert G. Roberge (Owner) 30 Merrimack Street (Sheet 63 Lot 11) 
requesting variance from Land Use Code Section 190 -264 to exceed 
maximum accessory use area, 40% permit ted – 78% proposed – to 
construct a 30’ x 35’ three-car garage. RA Zone, Ward 3. 
 
Mr. Minkarah recused himself from this case. Steve Lionel was 
chosen as Chair Pro Tem. 
 
Voting on this case: 
 
JP Boucher 
Steve Lionel 
Joseph Patry 
 
Robert Roberge, 30 Merrimack Street, Nashua, NH. Mr. Roberge stated 
that the lot is accessed from Artillery Lane behind Holman Stadium. 
He stated a concrete pad has existed on the site for years. Mr. 
Lionel noted that while the garage is large, the lots on Merrimack 
Street are small and the houses are modest, which causes the 40% 
limit to be exceeded. 
 
Xavier Castacio, Mr. Roberge’s son. Mr. Castacio stated the family 
are car enthusiasts and require the three -car garage to protect 
their assets. He shared that a family vehicle had previously caught 
fire due to fireworks from Holman Stadium, making the garage a 
necessity for safety and protection. 
 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR:  
Three letters of support were received from neighbors: Heron 
Rodriguez (28 Merrimack St), Donna Gosselin (30 Merrimack St), and 
Jason Richwa (32-34 Merrimack St). 
 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR WITH QUESTIONS OR CONCERNS:
Zoning Board of Adjustment 
August 11, 2026 
Page 10 
 
 
 
No one. 
END OF PUBLIC HEARING, BEGINNING OF PUBLIC MEETING:  
The Board found the request consistent with the unusual 
neighborhood where garages are traditionally placed along 
Artillery Lane. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Boucher to approve the variance application. 
 
Mr. Boucher stated that granting the variance would not be contrary 
to the public interest as the garage addresses overcrowding on the 
lot and follows neighborhood patterns. 
 
Mr. Boucher stated the spirit of the ordinance would be observed  
because garages are normal for this neighborhood. 
 
Mr. Boucher s tated that substantial justice will be served  by 
allowing the owner to protect his vehicles from weather and fire 
hazards. 
 
Mr. Boucher stated property values will not be diminished. 
 
Mr. Boucher stated that unnecessary hardship exists  due to the 
narrow lot and the small size of the primary home relative to the 
proposed garage. He found the use reasonable. 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Patry.  
MOTION TO APPROVE CARRIED 3-0. 
 
 
6. Rachel Surrette & Justin Drohan (Owners) 19 Dublin Avenue (Sheet 
53 Lot 56) requesting variance from Land Use Code Section 190-209 
(C) to allow a driveway within 50 feet of an intersection – 38 
feet proposed, to remove existing driveway off of Dublin Avenue 
and construct new 24-foot wide driveway off of Dixville Street. R9 
Zone, Ward 1. 
 
Voting on this case: 
 
Jay Minkarah 
JP Boucher 
Steve Lionel 
Joseph Patry 
 
Justin Drohan, 19 Dublin Avenue, Nashua, NH. Mr. Drohan stated the 
goal is to move the driveway from an arterial road (Dublin Avenue)
Zoning Board of Adjustment 
August 11, 2026 
Page 11 
 
 
 
to a quiet dead-end street (Dixville Street) for safety. He noted 
that backing out of the current driveway onto Dublin Avenue is 
hazardous and that his truck often hangs into the road. The new 
24-foot driveway would accommodate four cars and be 38 feet from 
the intersection. He noted the neighbor at 17 Dublin already has 
a driveway 35 feet from the intersection. 
 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR:  
Jennifer Olson, 21 Dublin Avenue.  Ms. Olson stated she lives on 
the other side of Dixville Street and fully supports the project, 
noting that Dublin Avenue has become "crazy" with traffic. Letters 
of support were received from Kevin Kennedy (24 Dublin) and Ray 
Grier (22 Dublin). 
 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR WITH QUESTIONS OR CONCERNS:  
No one. 
 
END OF PUBLIC HEARING, BEGINNING OF PUBLIC MEETING:  
The Board found that putting the driveway on the dead-end Dixville 
Street was a significantly safer alternative. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Minkarah to approve the variance application. 
 
Mr. Minkarah stated that granting the variance would not be 
contrary to the pub lic interest  as it enhances public safety 
without changing neighborhood character. 
 
Mr. Minkarah stated the spirit of the ordinance would be observed 
because the 50 -foot setback rule is intended for safety, which 
this proposal achieves more effectively than  the current 
configuration. 
 
Mr. Minkarah stated that substantial justice will be served  by 
improving the owners’ access and safety. 
 
Mr. Minkarah stated property values will not be diminished, citing 
neighbor support. 
 
Mr. Minkarah stated that unnecessary hardship exists due to the 
lot’s location and size, making it impossible to install a standard 
driveway that meets the setback. He found the use reasonable. 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Lionel.  
MOTION TO APPROVE CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY 4-0.
Zoning Board of Adjustment 
August 11, 2026 
Page 12 
 
 
 
 
 
7. Blue Coral Cross, LLC (Owner) Anand Mahendrakar (Applicant) 19 
Cross Street (Sheet 42 Lot 115) requesting variance from Land Use 
Code Section 190-16, Table 16-3 for minimum land area, 6,110 sq.ft 
exists – 20,909 sq.ft required – to convert an existing 3 -unit 
residential building into a 6-unit residential building. RC Zone, 
Ward 3. 
 
Voting on this case: 
 
Jay Minkarah 
JP Boucher 
Steve Lionel 
Joseph Patry 
 
Anand Mahendrakar, Blue Coral Cross, LLC. Mr. Mahendrakar amended 
the request during testimony, seeking to remodel the building into 
five units rather than six. He stated the remodel would be interior 
only and that the property already has eight paved parking spots 
in tandem. He expressed willingness to work with the city on 
landscaping and drainage. He provided context showing other six -
unit buildings on Cross Street. Mr. Durfee clarified that state 
law now requires only a 1:1 parking ratio. 
 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR WITH QUESTIONS OR CONCERNS:  
A letter was received from Michelle Plant, 15.5 Cross Street, 
expressing concerns regarding snow storage, drainage, traffic, and 
noise. 
 
END OF PUBLIC HEARING, BEGINNING OF PUBLIC MEETING:  
Mr. Boucher and Mr. Lionel found the reduction to five units and 
the existing eight parking spots satisfied their concerns. Mr. 
Minkarah expressed pause regarding tandem parking with five 
different units but ultimately agreed the density was consistent 
with the neighborhood. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Patry to approve the variance for five units. 
 
Mr. Patry stated that granting the variance would not be contrary 
to the public interest  as the density is within neighborhood 
character. 
 
Mr. Patry stated the spirit of the ordinance would be observed.
Zoning Board of Adjustment 
August 11, 2026 
Page 13 
 
 
 
Mr. Patry stated that substantial justice will be served  by 
increasing the housing stock. 
 
Mr. Patry stated property values are likely to increase  with the 
added units. 
 
Mr. Patry stated that unnecessary hardship exists because of the 
lot’s location in a dense district and the minor nature of the 
increase. 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Boucher.  
MOTION TO APPROVE CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY 4-0. 
 
 
OTHER BUSINESS:  
 
REGIONAL IMPACT: The Board saw no cases with Regional Impact. 
 
MINUTES:  
 
July 28, 2026. Mr. Patry and Mr. Lionel noted several corrections: 
 
• Page 1: Buckmeadow Road cases were postponed to a date 
certain. 
• Page 2: "Keith Fredette" should be "Kevin Fredette". 
• Page 4: Strike out "is available" regarding NH Fish and Game. 
• Page 9: Insert "driver" in the Joe Landry paragraph. 
• Page 11: Add a missing period.  
 
MOTION by Mr. Lionel to approve the minutes as amended.  
SECONDED by Mr. Patry.  
MOTION CARRIED 4-0. 
 
ADJOURNMENT:  
MOTION by Mr. Lionel to adjourn at 8:24 PM.  
SECONDED by Mr. Minkarah.  
CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY 
 
 
Submitted by:  Mr. Durfee, Clerk.
